claim: Past a task- and model-specific length, extra sequential reasoning tokens lower accuracy (gain, plateau, mild decline). Seen in R1-32B/s1-32B on AIME and GPQA, R1-distill on GSM8K, Qwen2.5 on MATH L5, and 9 frontier models on constructed tasks. Gap search 2026-11: closed frontier models (GPT-5, o3, Gemini 2.5) show a plateau on basic maths, not a decline, and Qwen3-235B improves smoothly to 32K on the vendor's plots; the drop is model- and task-specific. Zhou used greedy decoding, no seeds, no paired test.
agent_test: Sweep our agent's thinking budget at 4+ levels on one set; plot accuracy vs tokens and find the peak.

claim: The decline is small in the best-measured natural-difficulty setting (R1-32B AIME: 55.8 at 12K to 54.9 at 16K, about 0.5 problem of 60) but large in constructed tasks (Opus 4 100 to 85-90, R1 70 to 30) and Wait-forcing on small models (87.3 to 70.3). Magnitude depends on setup. Zhou ran one greedy pass per model, so no seed or paired test backs the 0.9-point drop.
agent_test: Report size of drop with CI; require paired problems and several seeds before acting on a decline.

claim: Optimal reasoning length rises with problem difficulty (MATH L1 about 1K vs L5 about 7.5K) and falls with model size (Qwen2.5 14 steps at 1.5B to 4 at 72B). A fixed budget is wrong for some tasks.
agent_test: Route by difficulty estimate and compare adaptive budget vs fixed budget at equal mean tokens.

claim: Hand audit: 67.5% of 80 R1 negative flips are genuine abandonment of a correct answer; 20% exploration divergence; 12.5% degradation artifacts (single model, authors coded). Gap search: Zeng finds revision success under 10% and failed revision above successful for QwQ and R1-1.5B; Shen shows a same-model judge picks the later answer in over 95% of disagreements.
agent_test: Log cases where our agent changes a correct answer after revision; code them.

claim: Trace signals (answer oscillation r=0.78, combined r=0.82, precision 76.3% at 80% recall) predict negative flips; evaluated on the same sample used to define them. Gap search: no held-out test found. Bulut shows pooled probe scores can be pure difficulty (0.873 trace-blind, 0.496 within problem); ADT shows switching goes with lower accuracy across 16 small models.
agent_test: Build an oscillation counter on intermediate answers; test as stop trigger on held-out items.

claim: Early exit when an intermediate answer is stable or probe-confirmed cuts tokens 19-80% (up to 24% with probe, over 40% with answer-consistency) at about equal accuracy. Gap search: DEER beat full length on three models in math (e.g. Qwen3-14B 83.7 vs 82.8 at 57% tokens). An independent test on 7 non-math-heavy benchmarks with Qwen3-4B/8B found DEER and Dynasor did not raise accuracy (70.77 to 67.76; 72.50 to 70.64 for DEER). A learned stop head beat validation-chosen fixed budgets in WebShop (42.8 vs 35.0). Wins on math and agents with trained or tuned stops; no win with a simple rule outside math.
agent_test: Add answer-convergence stop; compare tokens and accuracy vs full run.

claim: Within one question, shorter sampled chains are more often correct than longer ones (GPQA-D: 69.1 vs 57.6 LN-Super-49B; up to 34.5 points). short-m@k matches majority vote with up to 40% fewer tokens. Gap search: the within-question gap holds in every difficulty tercile (LN-Super-49B easy 5.3k correct vs 11.1k wrong; hard 12.4k vs 16.8k tokens).
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare short-3@k, majority vote and our scaffold.

claim: At equal token budget, parallel sampling plus vote beats extending a single chain (up to 20-22% higher at 16K; GSM8K 1.5B +10.1 vs -11.8). Gap search: short-m@k beats majority vote at equal compute in four models (short-3@k +2% at 80k tokens on QwQ-32B), but majority wins at high compute for short-1@k in three of four models.
agent_test: Equal-token test: one long chain vs k short chains with vote.

claim: Skipping the thinking block beats thinking at small matched budgets (AMC23 at 700 tokens 51.3 vs 28.9); parallel NoThinking approaches Thinking with up to 9x lower latency. Gap search: confirmed at matched tokens for R1-Distill-Qwen-32B only; Thinking wins at about 3,500 tokens pass@1 and on LiveCodeBench.
agent_test: Test a no-thinking first pass for easy items at equal tokens.

claim: On trivial questions o1-like models burn far more tokens (1,953% on 2+3); the first solution is correct in over 92% of correct cases and uses 38.7% of tokens on ASDIV.
agent_test: Measure fraction of our agent tokens spent after the first correct answer.

claim: Self-training on shortened first-correct-plus-reflection traces cuts tokens with about equal accuracy (ASDIV 741.8 to 381.6 tokens, 96.9 to 96.8; MATH500 -48.6% in abstract, SimPO -22.3% in a different comparison).
agent_test: Out of scope for scaffold; use only as a target length profile.

claim: In agentic coding, high overthinking score correlates with fewer resolved issues; picking the lowest-overthinking of 2 low-effort o1 runs gave 27.3% at $800 vs 29.1% at $1,400 for high effort. But a single low-effort run was only 21.0%. Gap search: no new controlled agent evidence on harm; an agent-framework note (d23) is descriptive only.
agent_test: Cap planning-only turns; compare to unrestricted at equal cost.

claim: Opposite failure is real: wrong answers use 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches; penalising switches raised AIME24 pass@1 (QwQ 38.3 to 44.1). Underthinking and overthinking coexist, so length alone is a poor proxy.
agent_test: Track switching rate and answer oscillation separately from length.

claim: Budget forcing with Wait raised s1-32B AIME24 from 50 to 57 and MATH500 fell 93.0 to 90.2 in some settings: extension helps on hard sets and can hurt on easier ones.
agent_test: Run Wait-style extension on hard and easy slices separately.

claim: Collapse of reasoning models on high-complexity puzzles ('Illusion of Thinking') is partly a token-limit and scoring artifact (Lawsen reply); not clean evidence for overthinking.
agent_test: Do not rely on it; use only controlled-budget evidence.

claim: CoT itself helps mainly on math/symbolic tasks (avg +12-14 points) and can hurt on some tasks (o1-preview 57.7 vs GPT-4o direct 94.0 on artificial grammar).
agent_test: Gate deliberation by task type at equal tokens.

claim: Longer reasoning can shift stated behaviour: Claude Sonnet 4 willing-to-be-turned-off 60% to 47% at up to 16,384 tokens; o3 differs. Gap search: Gema's own text shows 3 seeds and five budgets, and o3 (72 to 76%) and R1 (71-72%) do not show the Sonnet drop. No outside replication found.
agent_test: Check safety-eval stability across budgets.

claim: Wait-forcing early gain may be a variance artifact and later decline tied to rising output entropy (Ghosal); not proven causal. Gap search: Ghosal covers only 1.5B, 7B and 8B distilled models.
agent_test: Measure entropy of answer distribution across budgets.

claim: Natural long traces (no forcing) show the same decline as forced ones (R1-32B 54.2 to 47.3 across 6-8K to 12-16K; flip ratio 1.31 vs 1.42), though natural lengths are selected by difficulty and so confounded.
agent_test: Use natural-length vs forced comparisons with difficulty matched.

claim: Closed frontier models do not show a decline when effort is raised on basic maths: GPT-5 97% at medium and high effort, o3 97% at low, medium and high (8% more tokens), Gemini-2.5-Flash 92/93/92. Qwen3-235B improves to 32K on vendor plots. Overthinking on these is waste, not damage, at the coarse effort steps tested.
agent_test: Sweep our own model's budget on our own tasks in 3+ steps; log accuracy and tokens; do not assume a peak.

claim: Stop rules built on answer confidence or stability do not carry across domains: DEER gains in math (Qwen3-14B 83.7 vs 82.8) but loses on Qwen3-4B/8B across 7 benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 68.00 to 63.14; MuSiQue 59.00 to 51.67). Dynasor used 1.26-1.52x tokens.
agent_test: Validate any stop rule per task type on held-out items before using it.

claim: A model asked to choose between its own earlier and later answer picks the later one in over 95% of disagreements (MuSR 97.7%, MMLU-Pro 95.1%) and is right on the earlier-correct cases 0.0% and 6.7% of the time, at near 100% confidence. A verify-before-revise gate cannot be the same model reading the two answers. Independent re-solving by other models worked at about 2.6x tokens.
agent_test: Make the revise gate an external check or an independent re-solve, never self-comparison; log rescued vs harmed answers.

claim: Trace indicators must be validated within problem. A trace-blind difficulty proxy reaches AUROC 0.873 on 192K R1 generations; a matched reconstruction of a published probe drops from 0.849 pooled to 0.496 within problem. Zhou's r=0.78 was pooled and tested on its defining sample.
agent_test: Evaluate any oscillation counter by within-problem lift over a difficulty baseline.

claim: In closed-loop agent tasks a learned stop head matched full thinking at less cost (WebShop Qwen3.8-27B: 42.8 at 3464 tok/ep vs 43.0 at 5945) and beat validation-chosen fixed budgets (35.0 at 1519). On WebShop with Nemotron it beat full thinking (37.0 vs 34.5). Gaps are within about one seed SD.
agent_test: If we add a stop rule for agent steps, train or tune it on held-out episodes and compare with a fixed budget at matched success.

claim: As of November 2026 no paper was found that replicates or fails to replicate Zhou et al.'s flip-ratio findings. Of 21 citing papers listed, the five closest cite it as motivation only.
agent_test: Treat Zhou's thresholds (7K crossover, 12K peak) as unreplicated; measure on our own agent.

claim: Across 16 open models and 4 benchmarks, higher-accuracy model-task pairs switch their dominant answer less and commit earlier (switching -0.68 SD, commitment -0.53 SD); short-CoT pairs switch more. Switching is a cross-model signal, but the Wang switch-penalty result (QwQ 38.3 to 44.1) has no budget sweep, so over and underthinking are not yet traded off in one curve.
agent_test: Log answer switches per trace; test a switch cap with a stop rule across a budget sweep.
